name: Surface and Mesh Extraction
text:
# Surface and Mesh Extraction

Also called: Gaussian Mesh Extraction, 3DGS Meshing

## Overview
This family provides methods to convert a trained [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) radiance field into a explicit triangular mesh or segmented 3D structure. Standard 3DGS represents scenes as opaque/colored primitives, lacking explicit surface topology [Surface and Mesh Extraction](8498-surface-and-mesh-extraction.md). These extensions solve the problem of obtaining watertight, textured meshes or editable semantic segments from the implicit density fields of Gaussians, enabling applications in CAD, virtual reality, and scene editing. They differ from standard rendering by outputting geometric primitives (triangles) or semantic labels rather than pixel colors.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the standard 3DGS [primitive representation](#11838-primitive-representation.md): a set of $M$ anisotropic 3D Gaussian kernels $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$ [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md). Each kernel is defined by:
*   $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$: Position (mean) [S1].
*   $\mathbf{R}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$: Rotation matrix [S1].
*   $\mathbf{S}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$: Scale matrix [S1].
*   The covariance matrix is $\mathbf{\Sigma}_i = \mathbf{R}_i \mathbf{S}_i \mathbf{S}_i^\top \mathbf{R}_i^\top$ [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

The rendering pipeline's geometric projection remains consistent for ray-based methods: 3D Gaussians are transformed into ray space, and the projected 2D covariance $\mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i$ is computed using the Jacobian $J$ of the affine approximation of the projection and the rotation part $W$ of the extrinsic matrix:
$$ \mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i = J W \mathbf{\Sigma}_i W^T J^T $$
[Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md)

However, the attribute representation and loss functions diverge significantly from the standard RGB opacity/color model. Standard 3DGS uses view-dependent color $\mathbf{c}_i(\mathbf{d})$ [G]. In radiative and domain-specific variants, this is replaced by view-independent scalar attributes or feature vectors [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md), [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md].

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
Extracts a mesh by building a volumetric density field from Gaussian opacities and applying marching cubes. Chosen when a direct, training-free conversion from opacity to surface is required.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
Aligns Gaussians to a pre-existing mesh using distance-based classification (tight/loose) and [normal consistency](#3050-normal-consistency.md) losses. Chosen when high-fidelity geometric alignment to a known topology is needed, reducing redundancy.

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
Segments Gaussians by lifting 2D SAM masks from reference views into 3D via multi-view voting. Chosen for training-free semantic editing of specific scene parts.

### [Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction](12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md)
Extracts a mesh by rendering depth/normal maps to create an oriented point cloud, then applying Poisson reconstruction. Chosen when high-fidelity surface topology is required from a radiance field lacking explicit geometric regularization.

## Background
3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md). While efficient for novel view synthesis, the Gaussian primitives are not surface-aligned, making mesh extraction non-trivial. Subsequent works like [GOF](#5992-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof.md) [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md], MeshGS [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md], and Poisson-based methods [12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md] emerged to bridge the gap between [implicit radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) and explicit mesh representations, enabling broader industrial and creative applications.
